I farm the way I always have: I start from what worked last year, then I shift a little if the weather, price, or labor pushes me. I have 15 mu, and with wheat-maize as my main road, I will keep most land on that because grain feeds the house and brings steady money. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan and the crop goes thin, that hurts more than carrying a little extra fertilizer into the field. Around here, when I see neighbors get a full stand and good ears or good bolls, I remember what they used and stay close to that.

For wheat, I will keep the biggest piece, 10 mu. Wheat on our land with well water can still give a solid harvest if I feed it enough at sowing and again later. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I have seen cleaner heads and more even seedlings that way. I will water about 3 times if the season is normal: once after sowing if the ground is dry, once at jointing, once around grain filling. For summer maize on the same 10 mu, I will go right after wheat harvest and not waste days. I will use hybrid seed because that is what gives a full ear here. I will leave a little less fertilizer than wheat but still not light, because maize eats fast in hot weather. For the other 5 mu, I will spread risk: 2 mu cotton, 1.5 mu peanut, 1.5 mu mungbean. Cotton costs more in sprays, but if the stand is good it still brings cash. Peanut gives oil crop money and does well if I keep the base fertilizer strong. Mungbean I keep as a lighter crop: less fertilizer, fewer waterings, less money tied up. That way I do not put all my money into one thing, and if one crop goes bad, the whole year is not lost.
